module: Module 1 — Choose Who Appears On Camera

questions.q: Which are the two routes for an AI spokesperson in this course?
options: Your own likeness, or a properly licensed fictional spokesperson.
Your own likeness, or a colleague's.
A celebrity look-alike, or a stock photo of a real person.
questions.why: Only you, or a fictional character you have commercial rights to.

questions.q: A real person's photos are publicly available online. Does that give you permission to clone them?
options: Yes, if the photos are public.
No; public availability isn't permission, and providers require the person's own consent.
questions.why: Consent comes from the person, not from where the image is posted.

questions.q: Per HeyGen's help center (checked Oct. 23, 2026), who records the consent video for a digital twin?
options: The person whose avatar is being created.
questions.why: The consent video must feature the same person as the footage.

questions.q: A fictional spokesperson says, "When I sold my first home..." What's wrong?
options: It's a firsthand experience the character didn't have.
questions.why: Fictional spokespeople don't claim real experiences or licenses.

questions.q: Which disclosure approach does this module recommend?
options: An on-screen "Made with AI" label plus a plain line in the caption.
A disclosure only in your profile bio.
questions.why: Visible and plain, on every video.

questions.q: Can students use Eva Vail as their spokesperson?
options: No; the course grants no rights to copy AiRE Estate Academy's presenters, their voices, or its owner.
questions.why: Your spokesperson must be yours.

questions.q: Do your brokerage's advertising rules apply to AI avatar videos?
options: Yes; brokerage identification and required disclosures still apply.
Only if the video is longer than a minute.
questions.why: AI is a production method, not an exemption.

questions.q: Why lock a master look?
options: Repeated videos feel like one recognizable person; small changes compound.
questions.why: Consistency builds recognition.

questions.q: Which change is controlled?
options: New jacket, new hair and new background together.
Only the background changes; everything else stays the same.
New framing, new outfit and outdoor light.
questions.why: One element at a time.

questions.q: Per HeyGen's filming guidance (checked Oct. 23, 2026), what minimum recording quality is suggested?
questions.why: Higher (e.g., 4K, 60 fps) is better, but 1080p/30 is the floor.

questions.q: You stumble on a word during your recording. What does HeyGen's guidance say to do?
options: Stop, cut out the mistake, and splice the clip.
Keep speaking naturally or restart from the beginning; don't stitch clips.
questions.why: The footage must be one continuous recording.

questions.q: Why avoid clothing with large logos or text?
options: It can cause artifacts or distortions in the avatar, and distracts from you.
questions.why: HeyGen's FAQ notes logos and text may cause artifacts.

questions.q: What may students take from the Eva Vail example?
options: The method: lock identity, vary the setting.
questions.why: Copy the method, never the person.

questions.q: How many planned settings does this module suggest starting with?
questions.why: Two controlled settings are plenty to start.

module: Module 3 — Set Up the Voice and Delivery

questions.q: Why test pronunciation with a short preview before rendering a full video?
options: It catches most problems cheaply, before spending on a full render.
questions.why: Short previews are the cheap place to find problems.

questions.q: The voice says "HAIR-on Point" instead of the local "Heron Point." What's the fix?
options: Respell it in the spoken script (or use a pronunciation setting), keep the caption correct, and preview again.
questions.why: Spoken script and caption serve different jobs.

questions.q: Which voice is authorized for a fictional spokesperson?
options: A voice that imitates a famous actor.
A stock or licensed voice whose terms allow commercial use.
questions.why: Keep the license.

questions.q: Per HeyGen's guidance (Oct. 23, 2026), why should your filming footage include you speaking even if you'll use a different voice?
questions.why: The help center flags speech in footage as crucial for lip sync.

questions.q: How should you write "$612,000" in the spoken script?
options: The way you want it said, e.g., "six hundred twelve thousand dollars," while the caption shows "$612,000."
questions.why: Spell numbers for speech; keep figures correct in captions.

questions.q: Where should you test playback most carefully?
options: A phone speaker at normal volume, where most viewers listen.
questions.why: Plus laptop and headphones.

questions.q: Voice consent requirements and features...
options: Should be verified with the provider before you rely on them.
Are the same at every provider.
questions.why: Check current terms and features in your account.

module: Module 4 — Write a Short Script That Holds Attention

questions.q: Which is the strongest hook for sellers?
options: "Selling in Willow Fork next year? Start here."
"So, um, today I wanted to talk about something."
questions.why: It tells the right viewer it's for them, in the first seconds.

questions.q: You have three tips. What should you do?
options: Make three videos, one point each.
questions.why: One useful point per video.

questions.q: An AI draft says "Homes with HOA documents ready sell 22% faster." You have no source. What do you do?
options: Delete it, or replace it with careful general wording.
questions.why: Unsourced statistics don't go in your videos.

questions.q: How should you determine a script's length?
options: Read it aloud at the spokesperson's pace and time it.
questions.why: Word counts are only a starting guess.

questions.q: Which line belongs in a fictional spokesperson's script?
options: "My clients always tell me..." (no real quote)
"Before you list, find your HOA documents."
questions.why: Useful and true; no invented experiences, testimonials or guarantees.

questions.q: A listing invitation states the HOA fee as "$40/month." The fee isn't confirmed. What's the problem?
options: It's an unconfirmed fact; leave it out until it's documented.
questions.why: Facts come from approved sources only.

questions.q: How many calls to action should a 20-second video have?
questions.why: Two CTAs compete; one gets done.

questions.q: In HeyGen's own-likeness flow (checked Oct. 23, 2026), which option creates an avatar of you?
questions.why: From Avatars → New Avatar.

questions.q: According to HeyGen's help center, how often can you recreate an avatar in the same slot?
questions.why: And deleting an avatar removes all its looks, so fix footage before uploading.

questions.q: Which aspect ratio fits Reels, Stories and TikTok?
questions.why: Vertical.

questions.q: Lip sync drifts on one long sentence. What's the best first fix?
options: Split the sentence and re-render once.
questions.why: Diagnose, make one change, re-render.

questions.q: The face looks wrong in every video. Where's the likely problem?
options: The source footage; re-rendering won't fix it.
questions.why: Fix the footage at the source.

questions.q: Why does this course favor a stationary presenter with B-roll cuts over an avatar walking around?
options: Natural, stationary delivery with purposeful cuts holds up better than repeated artificial walking.
questions.why: Movement should have a purpose.

questions.q: What's the rule for re-rendering the same problem?
options: Two attempts, then stop and diagnose.
questions.why: Endless re-rendering costs money without fixing causes.

questions.q: Where should captions sit on a vertical social video?
options: In the middle band, clear of the platform's buttons and text.
questions.why: Bottom and right edges are often covered by platform UI.

questions.q: Auto-captions spelled the street "Herring Point." What should you do?
options: Correct every caption by hand against the script and source.
questions.why: Automated transcription is a start, not a finish.

questions.q: How loud should music be?
options: Clearly under speech; every word understandable on a phone speaker.
questions.why: Speech first.

questions.q: Why export three separate 9:16 videos instead of one merged grid?
options: Separate files let you post, test and fix each one independently.
questions.why: One idea, one video, one file.

questions.q: A caption shows a detail the voice didn't say. What's the issue?
options: Captions must match the spoken facts; a mismatch invites errors and confusion.
It should be in a different color.
questions.why: Not more, not less.

questions.q: Which B-roll is appropriate for a real listing video?
options: Any home photo from the internet.
Listing photos you're authorized to use, with fact cards matched to the listing sheet.
Photos of a different, nicer house.
questions.why: Permission and accuracy.

questions.q: Why keep a clean version (no captions or music)?
options: To make future edits without re-rendering the talking video.
questions.why: It saves time and credits later.

questions.q: What is a "production kit" in this course?
options: Your saved templates plus all your sheets and checklists, kept together.
questions.why: It makes the next video faster and consistent.

questions.q: You want a winter look. What's the right approach?
options: Change wardrobe, hair and background together.
Add a planned setting that changes one element; test against the master.
questions.why: Controlled variation keeps identity.

questions.q: Why batch production?
options: It saves setup time and lets you check facts in one focused pass.
questions.why: Efficiency and accuracy, no guarantees.

questions.q: When can a calendar row be marked "Approved"?
options: As soon as the script is written.
After the finished file passes all checks and you've reviewed it on your phone.
When a colleague likes the topic.
questions.why: Approval follows review of the finished video.

questions.q: A saved listing template contains last week's open-house time. What does this tell you?
options: A template doesn't validate its claims; every new video needs fact checks.
questions.why: Templates save time, not verification.

questions.q: What can platform analytics tell you?
options: Exactly how the next video will perform.
What happened with past videos, to inform your next topics and hooks.
questions.why: Numbers describe; they don't promise.

questions.q: Which statement is consistent with this course?
options: "No template or posting time guarantees views, leads or listings."
questions.why: Measure, learn and adjust; don't promise.
